text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Niger President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara discuss bilateral cooperation in agriculture and trade. The Niger president says that Mubarak is a voice of Africa. The two sides hold extensive talks including extension of Egypt's experience in agricultural, mining and industry.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi says that the opening of a United States Federal Bureau of Investigation office in Cairo means it will be used for an exchange of information between the two countries in the security fields. He said that it does not mean an encroachment on Egypt's sovereignty.
- President receives the papers of 14 new ambassadors.
- Egypt welcomes France's role in the peace process, says adviser Osama al-Baz.
- Mubarak will arrive in Washington on March 8.
- Mubarak recives a letter from the Yemeni president, and accepts an invitation to visit Yemen at a time to be determined.
- Four new paper processing industries to be set up with investment worth two billion pounds.
- Alfi says that Egypt's emergency law is not an "innovation" different from other countries also fighting terrorism.
- Tunisia and Egypt to discuss ten new accords to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
- Investment law to be debated by the economic committee; it could give a 20 year tax exemption for projects in the new river project.
